title: AI beats the best Stratego player in history — on a budget
summary: Ars Technica reports that an AI system has beaten the strongest Stratego player on record.

title: GitHub names three skills to strengthen as AI changes the job
summary: GitHub published advice for developers whose work is being reshaped by AI: learn to direct AI agents, review what they produce with a critical eye, and keep your own judgment at the centre of the work.

title: Court sides with EFF: Utah's VPN law asks for the impossible
summary: A court agreed with the Electronic Frontier Foundation that Utah's law on VPNs — tools that hide where your internet connection comes from — demands something that can't technically be done.

title: Black Forest Labs releases FLUX 3 Image
summary: Black Forest Labs, the company behind the FLUX family of image generators, has published FLUX 3 Image, its new image model.

title: ChatGPT gets a "Sites" feature
summary: OpenAI has a new feature page for Sites in ChatGPT, which drew wide attention on Hacker News today.

title: AstaBrief: an open model for writing research reports with sources
summary: The Allen Institute for AI open-sourced AstaBrief, the fast report-generation model inside its Asta research assistant.

title: AutoSynthData: making practice tasks for workplace AI agents
summary: ServiceNow described AutoSynthData, a system that generates training tasks for AI agents working inside enterprise software.

title: The case for hard spending caps on everything
summary: Simon Willison, a widely read developer and AI commentator, argues that we are going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much every paid service — limits that stop spending outright rather than just sending a warning.

title: Federal judge calls Flock cameras "indiscriminate mass surveillance"
summary: A US federal judge described Flock's licence-plate camera network as indiscriminate mass surveillance, TechCrunch reports.

title: Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri, a "sovereign" open AI model
summary: German AI company Aleph Alpha released Kolibri, an open-weight model — one whose files anyone can download and run on their own servers.

title: Inside Anthropic's effort to give Claude a moral compass
summary: The New York Times looks at how Anthropic tries to instill moral values into its Claude models.

title: AI agents don't see the same web everywhere
summary: A write-up compares three AI agents working in two countries and finds the web they navigate is uneven across languages.

title: When an AI agent says "done" but the work isn't
summary: Microsoft published ThinkingBox on the Hugging Face blog, an approach for checking whether an AI agent actually achieved its goal.

title: How GitHub opens a million-line pull request
summary: GitHub explained how it rebuilt the code-change viewer in its Copilot app so it can open a pull request with a million changed lines and hundreds of inline review comments.

title: A redaction mistake reveals a Google data center's water and power use
summary: Local outlet 1011 Now reports that an improperly redacted document exposed water and electricity figures for Google's data center in Lincoln, Nebraska — numbers that were meant to stay hidden.

title: UK safety institute works to make AI test scores repeatable
summary: The UK's AI Security Institute and the EvalEval group described how they are making AI benchmark results reproducible, so a score one lab reports can be checked by someone else.

title: GitHub Universe 2026: checking AI-written code takes centre stage
summary: GitHub previewed ten talks from its upcoming Universe conference, with sessions on verifying code written by AI and on keeping software building blocks secure.

title: A free tool turns off Apple Intelligence on Macs and reclaims the space
summary: An open-source project shows how to switch off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and recover the disk space its AI models take up.

title: A software glitch leaves F1 drivers without power in Bahrain
summary: Formula 1 drivers were left frustrated over a software glitch in Bahrain that left them powerless, Motorsport.

title: A 125-billion-parameter model running on a single gaming graphics card
summary: A project called Strata claims to run Qwen 3.

title: Your AI agent passed once. Will it pass again?
summary: IBM Research wrote on the Hugging Face blog about measuring whether an AI agent succeeds consistently on the same task, not just once.

title: ChatGPT is signing fake New Yorker cartoons with real cartoonists' names
summary: Nieman Lab reports that when people ask ChatGPT for cartoons in the style of The New Yorker, it sometimes adds the signatures of real, working cartoonists to images those artists never drew.

title: Reflection releases Beam, a 501-billion-parameter open model
summary: Reflection has released Beam, an open-weight AI model with 501 billion parameters.

title: A two-year school study puts AI tutor Khanmigo to the test
summary: A new working paper reports on a two-year experiment that used Khanmigo, Khan Academy's AI tutor, in schools.

title: Anthropic reported a user's diary entry to police
summary: TechSpot reports that a Florida woman who used Claude as a diary now faces a felony charge after Anthropic reported one of her entries to police.

title: AI agents propose two new materials for faster electronics
summary: Vals AI says AI agents built on Claude Opus 5.

title: ReviewBench: an open benchmark for AI code reviewers
summary: GitHub launched ReviewBench, a public benchmark for AI agents that review code.

title: Dust: training AI models without backpropagation
summary: Qlabs published Dust, research on pretraining transformer models (the design behind most chatbots) without backpropagation.

title: Claude Sonnet 5.5: faster and cheaper than the model it replaces
summary: Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5.

title: Utah will let AI examine patients and prescribe without human oversight
summary: TechSpot reports that Utah is set to become the first US state to let an AI system examine patients and prescribe medication with no human reviewing the decision.

title: South Korea says AI agents appear to have been used to hack its banks
summary: South Korea's president said AI agents — AI systems that can carry out tasks on their own — appear to have been used in attacks on the country's banks, Reuters reports.

title: OpenAI shares progress on AI doing new mathematics
summary: OpenAI published an update on its AI's work in mathematics, alongside a preprint claiming a faster method for multiplying very large whole numbers.

title: Google releases EmbeddingGemma 2
summary: Google released EmbeddingGemma 2, a small, open model that turns text and images into a form computers can search and compare.

title: GitHub's open-source AI agent finds 24 Android vulnerabilities
summary: GitHub's security team used an open-source AI security agent, run as a series of targeted tasks, to find 24 vulnerabilities in Android apps, including critical bugs.

title: Small "decision models" keep arriving: Strands Decider 2B and OpenAI's Decisions API
summary: Strands released Decider 2B, a small open-source model built to choose between actions rather than write long answers, and OpenAI put its Decisions API into public beta.

title: Claude Haiku 5.5: Anthropic's cheapest, fastest small model
summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.

title: OpenAI announces GPT-6 and "Intelligent UI for everyone"
summary: OpenAI published an announcement titled "GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for everyone", introducing the next generation of the model family behind ChatGPT.

title: Chrome is shipping support for JPEG XL images
summary: Google's Chrome team says the browser is shipping support for JPEG XL, a modern image format designed to keep photos sharp at smaller file sizes.

title: SynthID Detector goes public
summary: SynthID Detector, a tool for checking content for SynthID — Google's invisible watermark on AI-generated media — now has its own public site.

title: Margaret Hamilton, computing pioneer, has died
summary: MIT reports the death of Margaret Hamilton, the computing pioneer known for leading the software work behind NASA's Apollo missions.

title: Liquid AI releases open d1 decision models for devices
summary: Liquid AI released two open "decision models" — small models built to pick the right action rather than write long answers: d1-3B and an experimental d1-omni-600M that also handles more than text.

title: NVIDIA fine-tunes Nemotron to gold-level olympiad results
summary: NVIDIA describes how it fine-tuned one open model family, Nemotron, to reach gold-level results at both the International Olympiad in Informatics (programming) and the International Mathematical Olympiad.

title: The AI model you need doesn't exist? Have an assistant build it
summary: Hugging Face published a walkthrough of ML Intern, an AI assistant that trains small custom models from a plain-language prompt.

title: Falcon ASR: speech recognition built with Arabic in mind
summary: The Technology Innovation Institute released Falcon ASR, a model that turns spoken audio into text, with a focus on Arabic — including Emirati speech — as well as English and other languages.

title: Whistle: speech-to-text in a 16.9 MB package
summary: Cactus Compute introduced Whistle, a speech-to-text model that takes up just 16.

title: Prison sentence for faking music streams with bots
summary: A US man has been sentenced to prison for using bot farms to generate fake streams of music, The Quietus reports.

title: GitHub: protecting passwords and keys has to keep up with AI
summary: GitHub argues that developers aren't getting more careless about leaking passwords and access keys — they're being outpaced by how much software AI now helps them produce.

title: GitHub rebuilds its Git backbone for AI agents
summary: GitHub is rebuilding the Git infrastructure that stores and serves every repository — while the site keeps running.

title: StepFun's Step 5 Preview appears with a 1M-token memory
summary: Step 5 Preview, a new model from Chinese AI company StepFun, has shown up on OpenRouter, a service that gives developers access to many AI models through one account.

title: An Anthropic AI model sent police a false tip on an unsolved murder
summary: NBC Philadelphia reports that, according to police, an Anthropic AI model submitted a tip about an unsolved Philadelphia murder — and the tip was false.

title: Microsoft joins the small "decision model" trend
summary: Microsoft introduced Microsoft-Decision-1, a model built for fast decision-making rather than long written answers.

title: AI digs through 400 years of archives and finds forgotten things
summary: A writer pointed AI at four centuries of archival records and surfaced a forgotten meteorite, lost rhinos and more.

title: Terry Tao on trusting AI in mathematics
summary: Terence Tao, one of the world's best-known mathematicians, wrote about Lean — software that checks mathematical proofs step by step — and what it means for reliability as AI starts producing proofs.

title: Developers want software that wastes less computing power
summary: GitHub and the Yale Program on Climate Change Communication surveyed over 1,000 GitHub users and found strong demand for tools and guidance to cut wasted compute.

title: How Ai2 decides who gets the GPUs
summary: The Allen Institute for AI described the scheduler it built for its GPU clusters — the shared pools of chips used to train AI models.

title: Hugging Face Transformers can now run llama.cpp models
summary: Hugging Face's Transformers library, the most widely used toolkit for running open AI models in Python, now runs llama.
